doc.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06

title: Suhor on Burton's character and his own army absence
summary: Suhor was in the army during this time, worked with Burton occasionally, and describes him as a self-promoter who drove musicians away.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I went, excuse me, I was in the army for a while while he was, right around that time when you started playing with Burton. Then I came back and he had alienated a lot of the musicians and I'd work with him occasionally. In fact, my paycheck was being held up by the state of Louisiana during the integration time and if that hadn't been for Joe Burton, giving me a few bucks a night would be terrible. When I was at his club I would not have had money to feed my family at that time. But yeah, I was out of town for part of that but I was here doing a lot of Joe Burton's epic, as it were. He was more of a promoter and a self-promoter than a musician although he could have been a fine piano player but he was more interested in thrusting his ego around the place than in getting into the artistry and he hired good musicians as long as he could keep them.
He hired them and fuss at them.
Am I raging? No, he was like a real idiot.
I seem to remember something about him ending up with a television show in the area
